Practical Lab 11: Amazon Q Developer and AWS AI services
Overview
In this hands-on lab, you will set up Amazon Q Developer in your IDE and use it to build a simple application that integrates AWS AI services. You'll experience how AI-powered development tools can accelerate your workflow and explore key AWS AI capabilities.

Estimated time: 45-60 minutes

Prerequisites:

AWS account with appropriate permissions
Visual Studio Code or JetBrains IDE installed
Node.js 18+ installed
Basic knowledge of JavaScript/TypeScript
AWS CLI configured
Task 1: Amazon Q Developer setup
Estimated time: 15 minutes

Objective
Install and configure Amazon Q Developer in your IDE to experience AI-assisted coding.

Steps
Step 1: Install Amazon Q Extension
For Visual Studio Code:

Open VS Code
Go to Extensions (Ctrl+Shift+X / Cmd+Shift+X)
Search for "Amazon Q"
Click "Install" on the Amazon Q extension
Restart VS Code if prompted
For JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm):

Go to Settings/Preferences → Plugins
Search for "Amazon Q"
Click "Install"
Restart your IDE
Step 2: Authenticate with AWS
Click on the Amazon Q icon in your IDE sidebar
Choose one of the authentication methods:
AWS Builder ID (Free tier - recommended for this lab)
IAM Identity Center (if your organization uses it)
Follow the browser authentication flow
Return to your IDE once authenticated
Step 3: Verify Installation
Open the Amazon Q chat panel
Ask a simple question: "How do I create a Lambda function in Node.js?"
Verify you receive a response
Validation
 Amazon Q extension is installed and active
 Successfully authenticated
 Can interact with Amazon Q chat
 Code suggestions appear when typing
Task 2: Build an AI-powered sentiment analysis API
Estimated time: 30 minutes

Objective
Use Amazon Q Developer to help you build a serverless API that analyzes text sentiment using Amazon Comprehend.

Architecture
API Gateway → Lambda Function → Amazon Comprehend → Response

Steps
Step 1: Project Setup (5 minutes)
Create a new project directory:
mkdir sentiment-analyzer
cd sentiment-analyzer
npm init -y

Ask Amazon Q: "Set up a Node.js project with AWS SDK for Comprehend"

Install required dependencies:

npm install @aws-sdk/client-comprehend
npm install --save-dev @types/node

Step 2: Create Lambda Function with Amazon Q (10 minutes)
Create a new file: index.js

Use Amazon Q to generate code. Try these prompts:

"Create a Lambda function that analyzes sentiment using Amazon Comprehend"
"Add error handling for invalid input"
"Add support for batch sentiment analysis"
Your function should:

Accept text input from API Gateway event
Call Amazon Comprehend DetectSentiment API
Return sentiment (POSITIVE, NEGATIVE, NEUTRAL, MIXED) with confidence scores
Handle errors gracefully
Expected structure:

import { ComprehendClient, DetectSentimentCommand } from '@aws-sdk/client-comprehend';

const client = new ComprehendClient({ region: process.env.AWS_REGION || 'us-east-1' });

export const handler = async (event) => {
  // Your implementation with Amazon Q's help
};

Step 3: Add Input Validation (5 minutes)
Ask Amazon Q: "Add input validation to check text length and language code"

Implement validation:

Text must be between 1 and 5000 characters
Language code must be valid (en, es, fr, de, etc.)
Return appropriate error messages
Step 4: Test Locally (5 minutes)
Create a test file: test.js

Ask Amazon Q: "Create a test script to invoke the Lambda function locally"

Test with sample inputs:

const testCases = [
  { text: "I love this product! It's amazing!", languageCode: 'en' },
  { text: "This is terrible and disappointing.", languageCode: 'en' },
  { text: "The weather is okay today.", languageCode: 'en' }
];

Run tests:
node test.js

Step 5: Deploy to AWS (5 minutes)
Create IAM role for Lambda with Comprehend permissions

Ask Amazon Q: "Create AWS CLI commands to deploy this Lambda function"

Package and deploy:

zip -r function.zip index.js node_modules/

aws lambda create-function \
  --function-name sentiment-analyzer \
  --runtime nodejs18.x \
  --role arn:aws:iam::YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID:role/lambda-comprehend-role \
  --handler index.handler \
  --zip-file fileb://function.zip

Test deployed function:
aws lambda invoke \
  --function-name sentiment-analyzer \
  --payload '{"text":"I love AWS!","languageCode":"en"}' \
  response.json

cat response.json

Validation
 Lambda function created with Amazon Q assistance
 Function successfully calls Amazon Comprehend
 Input validation works correctly
 Local tests pass
 Function deployed to AWS
 Remote invocation returns correct sentiment analysis
Expected Output
{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "body": {
    "sentiment": "POSITIVE",
    "sentimentScores": {
      "Positive": 0.98,
      "Negative": 0.01,
      "Neutral": 0.01,
      "Mixed": 0.00
    },
    "text": "I love AWS!"
  }
}

Task 3: Explore Amazon Q features
Estimated time: 10 minutes

Objective
Experience key Amazon Q Developer capabilities.

Sub-tasks
Task 1: Code Explanation
Select your Lambda function code
Right-click → Amazon Q → Explain
Review the explanation provided
Task 2: Security Scan
Run Amazon Q security scan on your code
Review any findings
Ask Amazon Q to fix identified issues
Task 3: Generate Tests
Ask Amazon Q: "Generate unit tests for the sentiment analyzer function"
Review generated tests
Run tests and verify coverage
Task 4: Code Optimization
Ask Amazon Q: "Optimize this Lambda function for better performance"
Review suggestions (caching, connection reuse, etc.)
Implement one optimization
Task 5: Documentation
Ask Amazon Q: "Generate JSDoc comments for this function"
Review and apply documentation
Validation
 Successfully used code explanation feature
 Ran security scan and reviewed findings
 Generated unit tests
 Received optimization suggestions
 Added documentation with Amazon Q help
Deliverables (all or some of them)
Screenshot: Amazon Q installed and authenticated in your IDE
Code: Complete Lambda function with:
Sentiment analysis implementation
Input validation
Error handling
Tests
Documentation
Test Results: Screenshots or logs showing:
Local test execution
AWS Lambda invocation results
Security scan results
Optional task 1: Explore AWS AI services in Management Console
Estimated time: 30-45 minutes

Extend your learning by exploring additional AWS AI services through the AWS Console.

Optional Task 1: Amazon Rekognition - Image Analysis (10 minutes)
Objective: Detect objects and text in images.

Steps:

Navigate to Amazon Rekognition in AWS Console
Go to "Label detection" demo
Upload a sample image (or use provided samples)
Observe detected labels, confidence scores, and bounding boxes
Try "Text in image" detection with an image containing text
Experiment with "Face detection" and "Face comparison"
Questions to explore:

What confidence threshold would you use in production?
How would you handle images with multiple objects?
What use cases fit your current projects?
Optional task 2: Amazon Polly - text-to-Speech
Estimated time: 10 minutes

Objective: Convert text to natural-sounding speech.

Steps:

Navigate to Amazon Polly in AWS Console
Enter sample text: "Welcome to AWS AI services. This is a demonstration of Amazon Polly's neural text-to-speech capabilities."
Try different voices:
Neural voices (Joanna, Matthew, Amy)
Standard voices
Different languages
Experiment with SSML tags:
<speak>
  Hello! <break time="1s"/> 
  This is <emphasis level="strong">important</emphasis>.
  <prosody rate="slow">Speaking slowly now.</prosody>
</speak>

Download the audio file
Test speech marks for lip-syncing applications
Questions to explore:

Which voice sounds most natural for your use case?
How would you integrate this into an application?
What are the cost implications for high-volume usage?
Optional task 3: Amazon Translate - language translation
Estimated time: 10 minutes

Objective: Translate text between languages.

Steps:

Navigate to Amazon Translate in AWS Console
Test real-time translation:
Source: English
Target: Spanish, French, German, Japanese
Text: "AWS provides powerful AI services that help developers build intelligent applications without requiring deep machine learning expertise."
Try auto-detect source language
Test with technical terminology
Experiment with custom terminology:
Create a custom terminology file
Add domain-specific terms (e.g., "Lambda" → "Lambda" not translated)
Test translation with custom terminology
Questions to explore:

How accurate is technical term translation?
When would you use custom terminology?
How would you handle unsupported languages?
Optional task 4: Amazon Textract - document analysis
Estimated time: 10 minutes

Objective: Extract text and data from documents.

Steps:

Navigate to Amazon Textract in AWS Console
Upload a sample document:
Invoice or receipt
Form with key-value pairs
Table-based document
Run "Analyze Document" with:
Text detection
Form extraction
Table extraction
Review extracted data:
Key-value pairs
Table structure
Confidence scores
Download results in JSON format
Analyze the structure for programmatic processing
Questions to explore:

How would you handle low-confidence extractions?
What post-processing would improve accuracy?
How would you integrate this into a workflow?
Optional task 5: Amazon Bedrock - generative AI
Estimated time: 15 minutes

Objective: Experiment with foundation models for text generation.

Steps:

Navigate to Amazon Bedrock in AWS Console
Request model access (if not already enabled):
Claude (Anthropic)
Titan (Amazon)
Go to "Text playground"
Test different prompts:
Prompt 1 - Code Generation:

Write a Python function that validates email addresses using regex.
Include error handling and unit tests.

Prompt 2 - Content Summarization:

Summarize the following text in 3 bullet points:
[Paste a technical article or documentation]

Prompt 3 - Data Transformation:

Convert this JSON to a SQL CREATE TABLE statement:
{"users": {"id": "integer", "name": "string", "email": "string"}}

Compare responses from different models (Claude vs Titan)
Experiment with parameters:
Temperature (0.0 - 1.0)
Top P
Max tokens
Test with your own use case
Questions to explore:

Which model performs better for your use case?
How do temperature settings affect output?
What are the cost differences between models?
Deliverable: Comparison table of model responses and parameter effects.

Optional bonus challenge: Combine multiple AI services (30 minutes)
Estimated time: 30-45 minutes

Objective: Build a multi-service AI pipeline.

Scenario: Create a document processing pipeline that:

Extracts text from an uploaded image (Textract)
Translates the text to English if needed (Translate)
Analyzes sentiment of the content (Comprehend)
Generates a summary (Bedrock)
Steps:

Use Amazon Q to help design the architecture
Create a Step Functions workflow or Lambda orchestrator
Implement each service integration
Test with sample documents in different languages
Measure end-to-end latency
Troubleshooting
Amazon Q Not Responding
Check internet connection
Verify authentication status
Restart IDE
Check AWS service status
Lambda Deployment Fails
Verify IAM role has correct permissions
Check function package size (< 50MB)
Ensure runtime matches code (Node.js 18.x)
Review CloudWatch logs for errors
Comprehend API Errors
Verify text length (1-5000 characters)
Check language code is supported
Ensure IAM role has comprehend:DetectSentiment permission
Check service quotas
AWS Console Access Issues
Verify IAM user has console access
Check service is available in your region
Some services require explicit access request (Bedrock)

Explore Amazon Q's code transformation features for legacy code modernization
